t: Nasdaq slips into a correction as the Dow edges toward one
s: After Thursday’s sell-off the Nasdaq Composite is in a correction, a fall of 10% or more from a record close, according to Nacionale News. The Dow closed at 49,097.06, about 9.7% below its August record and roughly 183 points from correction territory, while the S&P 500 is 8.2% off its high.

t: Dow plunges 1,101 points as the sell-off spreads beyond AI stocks
s: US stocks fell hard on Thursday as investors sold AI and chip shares and then almost everything else, with analysts saying no single event set it off. The Dow closed down 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, at 49,097.06, the S&P 500 lost 2.02% to 7,175.83 for a sixth straight decline, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.25% to 23,879.20.

t: Nvidia gives up its post-earnings gain as the Dow drops 561 points
s: Nvidia reversed its initial post-earnings gains on Wednesday and closed down 2.89%, according to a Vistap Global market report. The Dow fell 561.25 points, or 1.11%, to 50,198.17 and the S&P 500 lost 0.23% for a fifth straight decline, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.42%.

t: Fed minutes show officials leaning toward more rate rises
s: Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s most recent meeting showed almost all officials judged more rate rises would likely be appropriate, according to live market coverage on 18 November. The Dow extended its losses after the release and closed 561.25 points lower.

t: Wall Street slides again as Nvidia and AI stocks lead the decline
s: US stocks fell again on Tuesday as Nvidia and other jittery AI shares led losses. The S&P 500 sank 1% after swinging between almost no change and a 1.7% loss, the Dow dropped 1.6% and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.7% in another unsettled session.

t: Bitcoin steadies near $65,000 after a steep November slide
s: Bitcoin traded near $65,017 at 8:15 a.m. ET on 17 November, about $1,004 above the previous morning, according to Fortune’s daily price tracker. The coin was priced near $73,938 on 11 November, so it remains well below early-November levels.

t: Sensex and Nifty keep climbing as investors rotate into India
s: Indian equities extended their climb on 17 November, with the Sensex and Nifty closing higher. Market reports pointed to lower crude prices, strong foreign investor buying and a rotation of money from global AI stocks into Indian shares. Both benchmarks had also gained more than half a per cent on Monday.

t: Nvidia shares drop after CEO Jensen Huang resigns
s: US stocks ended a volatile Thursday session slightly lower after Nvidia shares fell following CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported. The major indexes traded on both sides of unchanged, a semiconductor index lost 0.5% and US Treasury yields climbed.

t: Gold tumbles 2.8% as the dollar hits a 19-month high
s: Spot gold fell 2.77% to $3,877.04 an ounce on Thursday, Reuters reported, as the US dollar index reached a fresh 19-month high on rate-hike expectations. Brent crude settled at $95.82 a barrel, up 3.3%, while US West Texas Intermediate closed at $88.74, up 2.6%.

t: Dow and Nasdaq rally as investors return to tech
s: US stocks rose on 11 November as investors returned to a volatile technology sector. Reuters reported the Dow gained 254.60 points to 52,486.49, the S&P 500 added 98.45 points to 7,619.38 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 400.31 points to 25,466.19.
